Description: Prefer StatelessWidget over StatefulWidget when the widget does not manage mutable state. Stateless widgets are cheaper to build and easier to reason about.
Do: Use StatelessWidget for purely presentational widgets that receive all data via constructor.
Don't: Convert a widget to StatefulWidget just because it feels easier — keep state as high or as low as needed.
Code Bad: class MyLabel extends StatefulWidget { ... } // no mutable state needed

Description: Declare const constructors on widgets and use const at call sites. Flutter can short-circuit rebuilds for const widgets because they are canonicalised at compile time.
Do: Add const to every widget constructor that has no mutable fields and use const keyword at instantiation.
Don't: Omit const on leaf widgets. Even a single non-const Text() in a subtree forces an extra reconcile pass.

Description: Break large build methods into small single-purpose widgets rather than nesting dozens of anonymous builders. Each widget is a rebuild boundary.
Do: Extract reusable sub-trees into their own widget classes with meaningful names.
Don't: Put 200+ lines of widget tree inside a single build() method.

Guideline: Override == and hashCode for data classes
Description: When passing data objects to widgets Flutter uses equality to decide whether to rebuild. Custom == prevents unnecessary diffs.
Do: Implement == and hashCode on model classes passed to widgets or use package:equatable.
Don't: Rely on default identity equality for data objects used as widget inputs.
Code Good: @override bool operator ==(o) => o is User && o.id == id;
Code Bad: class User { String id; } // no == override

Description: Provide a Key (ValueKey / ObjectKey) to widgets inside dynamic lists so Flutter can reconcile element moves efficiently.
Do: Use ValueKey(item.id) on list item widgets when the list can be reordered or items removed.
Don't: Use index-based keys or omit keys in mutable lists — causes incorrect diffing.

Description: Use Provider / ChangeNotifierProvider for straightforward shared state that doesn't require complex async side-effects or state machines.
Do: Wrap the widget subtree that needs access with ChangeNotifierProvider and consume with context.watch or Consumer.
Don't: Reach for Bloc or Riverpod before trying Provider — start with the simplest tool that fits.
Code Bad: // passing CartModel 5 levels deep via constructors

Description: Use Riverpod when you need compile-safe providers outside the widget tree or need to combine async data streams cleanly.
Do: Declare providers at the top level as final variables and consume with ref.watch inside ConsumerWidget.
Don't: Mix Riverpod and Provider in the same project — pick one and standardise.
Code Bad: // global variable holding raw state without provider

Description: Use flutter_bloc when state transitions are driven by discrete events and you need an audit trail or replaying capability (e.g. multi-step forms and wizards).
Do: Map UI events to Bloc events; keep business logic inside the Bloc; keep UI inside BlocBuilder.
Don't: Put business logic directly inside BlocBuilder or onPressed callbacks when using Bloc.
Code Bad: // setState() containing order submission HTTP call

Description: setState is appropriate only for ephemeral local UI state (animation tick and input focus). Lift anything shared beyond one widget into a state management solution.
Do: Use setState for toggle animations or form field focus; use Provider/Riverpod/Bloc for data shared across routes.
Don't: Call setState to update a list that is read by multiple screens.

Description: Use Expanded inside Row/Column to let a child fill remaining space proportionally. Avoids unbounded constraint errors caused by Column inside Column.
Do: Wrap flexible children with Expanded or Flexible and provide flex ratios when proportional sizing is needed.
Don't: Give a fixed height to a widget inside an unbounded Column expecting to size itself intrinsically.

Description: Use SizedBox for fixed whitespace between widgets instead of Container with no decoration — it is lighter and communicates intent.
Do: Replace Container(width: 8) spacing shims with SizedBox(width: 8) or SizedBox(height: 16) between siblings.
Don't: Use Container() as a pure spacer — Container carries unnecessary overhead for spacing only.

Description: Use ConstrainedBox or BoxConstraints to express responsive min/max sizes rather than hard-coding platform-specific pixel values.
Do: Apply BoxConstraints.tightFor or ConstrainedBox for cards and dialogs that should adapt to content but stay within readable bounds.
Don't: Hard-code MediaQuery pixel math for every breakpoint — use constraints + LayoutBuilder instead.

Description: Use Stack and Positioned/Align for badges, overlays and tooltips rather than fighting Row/Column. Clearly name anchor alignment.
Do: Use Align or Positioned with named anchors (topRight and bottomLeft) for overlay elements.
Don't: Use Stack for sequential vertical or horizontal layouts — that is what Column/Row are for.

Description: Use LayoutBuilder to read parent constraints at build time and switch layouts between compact and expanded breakpoints.
Do: Use LayoutBuilder instead of MediaQuery.of(context).size inside widget build methods to stay constraint-aware.
Don't: Query screen size directly in deeply nested widgets — they get stale constraints.

Description: Mark widget subtrees const so Flutter skips diffing them entirely on parent rebuilds. This is the single highest-ROI Flutter performance technique.
Do: Audit leaf widgets with the Flutter DevTools Rebuild Stats tool and add const wherever state is not needed.
Don't: Assume const has no effect on performance — it directly reduces ElementTree reconciliation work.

Description: Wrap complex animated sub-trees in RepaintBoundary to isolate their GPU layer so only that layer repaints on each animation frame.
Do: Apply RepaintBoundary to heavy animated widgets (charts, carousels and particle effects) to keep parent layer clean.
Don't: Wrap every single widget in RepaintBoundary — too many layers waste GPU memory.
Code Bad: // AnimatedChart rebuilt on every parent setState

Description: Use ListView.builder or ListView.separated for lists longer than ~20 items so only visible items are built and laid out.
Do: Supply itemCount and an itemBuilder callback; use ListView.separated for dividers.
Don't: Use ListView(children: [...]) with hundreds of widgets — all are instantiated at once.

Description: Heavy computation inside didUpdateWidget or initState that triggers setState creates jank. Move computation to an async isolate or FutureBuilder.
Do: Cache computed values and only recompute when dependent inputs change using a selector or memoised getter.
Don't: Call setState inside initState synchronously after async work without using mounted check.

Description: Use go_router for URL-based navigation that supports deep linking, web URLs and nested routes with typed parameters.
Do: Define routes in a GoRouter configuration at app root; use context.go() or context.push().
Don't: Maintain a manual Navigator stack with pushNamed for apps that need deep link support.

Description: Pass identifiers to route builders and let the destination screen fetch/derive its data from state management. Avoids stale data and large serialised arguments.
Do: Pass item.id through route path parameters; destination reads from provider/repository.
Don't: Pass full model objects through Navigator.arguments — breaks with deep links and URL routing.

Description: Use GoRouter redirect and pop with a result to handle flows like auth gates or confirmation dialogs without coupling screens.
Do: Use context.pop(result) and router-level redirect logic for auth guards.
Don't: Use WillPopScope deprecated API for back navigation handling in new Flutter versions.

Description: Define a single ThemeData with a ColorScheme.fromSeed or ColorScheme.fromImageProvider and propagate via MaterialApp.theme. Avoid local hex literals scattered across widgets.
Do: Reference theme colors via Theme.of(context).colorScheme.primary etc. to support light/dark mode automatically.
Don't: Hard-code hex color values in widget files — breaks dark mode and redesigns.

Description: Use Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleLarge etc. instead of manual TextStyle to ensure consistent responsive type scale that respects accessibility text scaling.
Do: Map every text element to a semantic TextTheme slot (displayLarge, bodyMedium, labelSmall).
Don't: Specify font size in every Text widget without using TextTheme — defeats system font scaling.

Description: Enable Material 3 via ThemeData(useMaterial3: true) and use updated component tokens. M3 provides better accessibility defaults and adaptive components.
Do: Use ColorScheme.fromSeed and M3 components; test on both platforms with adaptive scaffold.
Don't: Mix Material 2 and Material 3 component styles in the same app.

Description: Always handle all three AsyncSnapshot states (waiting, error, data) in FutureBuilder. Missing error state shows a blank screen on network failure.
Do: Show a loading indicator on ConnectionState.waiting and a retry widget on error; display data only when snapshot.hasData.
Don't: Return an empty Container from FutureBuilder when snapshot has no data — hides errors silently.

Description: Never call an async function directly inside build(). Each rebuild creates a new Future that is never awaited or cancelled.
Do: Trigger async calls in initState, didUpdateWidget or user event handlers; expose results through state or a StreamBuilder.
Don't: Return a Future from inside build() and discard it — causes memory leaks and race conditions.

Description: Use StreamBuilder for continuously updating data sources like Firestore collections, WebSocket feeds or periodic timers.
Do: Close streams in dispose() if created manually; use keep-alive for expensive streams.
Don't: Poll with a Timer and call setState — use a stream and StreamBuilder instead.

Description: Wrap custom interactive widgets in a Semantics widget with meaningful label, hint and onTap properties so screen readers can announce and activate them.
Do: Provide label for what the element is, hint for what happens when activated and button: true for tappable custom widgets.
Don't: Use a GestureDetector without Semantics — it is invisible to TalkBack and VoiceOver.
Code Good: Semantics(label: 'Add to cart', button: true, child: GestureDetector(onTap: _add, child: ...))
